decisions.quote: The item-set response variability yielded mean crossmeasure correlations of r = .40 and .45 in T1 and T2, closely matching the preregistered expectation and conceptually replicating Baird et al. (2017). In contrast, the strict Baird-style reconstruction yielded considerably weaker mean correlations of r = .20 and .26. Given that the latter relied on substantially fewer responses within each variability component than Baird et al.’s original measures, these smaller associations should be interpreted in light of the reduced reliability expected from lower item counts.
decisions.reason: The authors explicitly conclude that their preregistered analysis conceptually replicated Baird et al. (2017) and strongly supported their conclusion, attributing weaker correlations in the exploratory strict reconstruction to lower reliability from fewer items. The shipped quote from the abstract describes the extension to task engagement rather than a mixed replication verdict.

decisions.quote: The present study addressed two preregistered questions concerning response variability and careless responding. First, we aimed to conceptually replicate Baird et al.’s (2017) finding that individual differences in response variability generalize across substantively different measures. Second, we examined how accurately established careless-responding indicators distinguish truthful from overtly and covertly careless responding.
decisions.reason: The study explicitly identifies only Baird et al. (2017) as the replicated target (RQ1), while RQ2 is an extension evaluating careless-responding indicators under monitored adherence (predicting in H2a that all indicators, including longstring, would detect overt carelessness). Goldammer et al. (2020) is cited as background literature and for post-hoc discussion comparison, not as a target original finding re-tested by this study.

parent_objection: The exclusion treats RQ2 as extension/background because only Baird is explicitly named in RQ1. Yet introduction says we aimed to conceptually replicate and extend key findings from the latter two strands (response styles and carelessness),explicitly describes Goldammer2020 longstring discrimination finding,and current study tests indicator accuracy with experimenter-rated adherence; discussion directly compares results with Goldammer. Under codebook,labels/background or extension wording do not decide target relationship. Inspect whether current paper actually retests a specific Goldammer2020 empirical finding,or merely develops/tests a different claim using its methods. Do not infer target merely from topical relevance or generic consistency either. Settle target1 independently with self-contained source evidence. Baird outcome successful remains accepted;no outcome revision requested for Baird.

shipped.title_o: The role of response styles in the assessment of intraindividual personality variability
shipped.outcome_quote: These findings indicate that response variability contains stable individual differences while also being sensitive to task engagement.

blind_target.authors: Baird, B. M., Lucas, R. E., & Donnellan, M. B.
blind_target.title: The role of response styles in the assessment of intraindividual personality variability.
blind_target.study_numbers_original_note: Introduction discusses relevant correlations in Study 1; replication aim is stated at paper level.
blind_target.evidence_quote: For this, we aimed to conceptually replicate Baird et al.’s (2017) findings that corrected response variability is correlated across different measures.
blind_target.outcome_quote: The present findings highlight that response variability should not be interpreted uniformly, but rather that individual differences in response variability were stable across repeated assessments, generalized across measures and even remained substantially consistent between truthful vs. careless experimental conditions. This strongly supports the conclusions by Baird et al. (2017) and Nestler et al. (2021) that response variability contains stable respondentspecific information.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Overall substantive verdict explicitly strongly supports the original conclusion. The strict reconstruction gives weaker correlations and incomplete significance but is still positive; authors attribute smaller effects to reduced reliability, rather than concluding the central finding fails.
